<s>Mahāyānasaṁgraha</s> (Compendium of the Mahāyāna)
<s>Prastāvanā</s> (Introduction) 1
In the <s>Abhidharma-mahāyāna-sūtra</s>, before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, by a <s>bodhisattva</s> well-entered into the <s>Mahāyāna</s>,
for the purpose of revealing the greatness of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>,

body.text: tham uktaṁ yad uta mahāyānam ārabhya buddhabhagava-
body.translated_text: it was stated that, with regard to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Bhagavāns</s>'
words are distinguished by ten kinds of special features.
<s>Prastāvanā</s> (Introduction) 2

Namely, the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Bhagavāns</s>' (1) words distinguished by the special feature of the basis of the knowable (<s>jñeyāśraya</s>); (2) words distinguished by the special feature of the characteristics of the knowable (<s>jñeyalakṣaṇa</s>); (3) the knowable —
words distinguished by the special feature of entry into the characteristics (<s>jñeyalakṣaṇapraveśa</s>); (4) the entry into that — words distinguished by the special feature of cause and
fruit (<s>tatpraveśahetuphalavśeṣa</s>); (5) the cause and fruit of that — words distinguished by the special
feature of the divisions of cultivation (<s>taddhetuphalabhāvanāprabheda</s>);
(6) therein, among those divisions of cultivation,
words distinguished by the special feature of higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>); (7) words distinguished by the special feature of higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>);
(8) words distinguished by the special feature of higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>); (9) the fruit of that — words distinguished by the special feature of
abandonment (<s>tatphalaprahāṇa</s>); (10) the fruit of that — words distinguished by the special feature of
knowledge (<s>tatphalajñāna</s>).
This teaching of the <s>sūtra</s>-passages reveals that the <s>Mahāyāna</s>
is the word of the <s>Buddha</s>.
<s>Prastāvanā</s> (Introduction) 3

body.text: katham udbhāvayati| - tathā hy etayā deśanayā śrā-
body.translated_text: How does it reveal this? — Because by this teaching, ten topics
not taught in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (Vehicle of Hearers) are taught from the standpoint of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Namely:
(1) the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness) is taught as the basis of the knowable; (2) the three
natures (<s>svabhāvas</s>) — the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>), the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>), and the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>) —
are taught as the characteristics of the knowable; (3) mere cognition (<s>vijñaptimātratā</s>) is taught as the entry
into the characteristics of the knowable; (4) the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) are taught as the cause and fruit of
that entry; (5) the ten <s>bodhisattva</s> stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) are taught as the divisions of cultivating
that cause and fruit; (6) the <s>bodhisattva</s> precepts (<s>saṁvara</s>)
are taught as the higher morality therein; (7) the <s>samādhis</s> such as <s>Śūraṅgama</s>, <s>Gaganagañja</s>, and others
are taught as the higher mind therein; (8) non-conceptual knowledge (<s>nirvikalpajñāna</s>) is taught as the higher
wisdom; (9) non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>) is taught as the fruit of abandonment
of that; (10) the three <s>Buddha</s>-bodies (<s>kāyas</s>) — the essential (<s>svābhāvika</s>),
the enjoyment (<s>sāṁbhogika</s>), and the emanation (<s>nairmāṇika</s>) — are taught as the fruit of knowledge of that.

body.text: etāni daśasthānāni śrāvakayānād viśiṣṭāni yāni bhagavatā
body.translated_text: These ten topics, which are superior to the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, have been
revealed by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> as supremely distinguished, and
taught with reference to <s>bodhisattvas</s>.
Therefore, concerning the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Bhagavāns</s>'
words distinguished by ten kinds of special features should be understood.
<s>Prastāvanā</s> (Introduction) 4
How, then, does this tenfold distinguished word of the <s>Tathāgata</s>
illuminate that the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is indeed the word of the <s>Buddha</s>,

body.text: na ca śrāvakayānaṁ mahāyānam iti pratiṣiddham| -
body.translated_text: without refuting that the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>? —

body.text: eteṣāṁ hi daśasthānānāṁ deśanā śrāvakayāne na dṛśyate
body.translated_text: Because the teaching of these ten topics is not found in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>,

body.text: mahāyāne tu dṛśyate| etāni daśasthānāni mahābodhisaṁ-
body.translated_text: but is found in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. These ten topics are conducive to the attainment of
great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>), well-established, favorable, and non-contradictory
for the attainment of omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>). Here are two verses:
The basis of the knowable, [its] characteristics, entry into that, the cause and fruit of
that, the divisions of that,

body.text: śikṣātrayaṁ tatphalaṁ ca prahāṇaṁ jñānaṁ cāgrayā-
body.translated_text: the threefold training, the fruit of that and abandonment, and knowledge — [all] gone to the foremost
vehicle — are distinguished. (1)

body.text: eṣā hi deśanānyatra na dṛśyate eteṣām uttamabodhihe-
body.translated_text: This teaching is not seen elsewhere; by showing that these are the causes of supreme awakening,
the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is accepted as the word of the <s>Buddha</s>, distinguished by the teaching of
the ten topics. (2)
<s>Prastāvanā</s> (Introduction) 5

body.text: kim artham eteṣāṁ daśasthānānām evaṁ kramo deśitaḥ
body.translated_text: For what purpose is this order of the ten topics taught?

body.text: | - (1) bodhisattvena hi prathamata eva tāvad dharmā-
body.translated_text: — (1) A <s>bodhisattva</s> should first of all, relying on

body.text: ṇāṁ hetau kauśalyaṁ niśritya pratītyasamutpāde kauśal-
body.translated_text: skill regarding the cause of <s>dharmas</s>, attain skill in
dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). (2) Then, regarding the dependently originated
<s>dharmas</s>, skill in their characteristics should be attained — through skill in avoiding the faults of
superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>) and denial (<s>apavāda</s>). (3) A <s>bodhisattva</s> thus engaged
should penetrate that well-grasped characteristic, and thereby the mind

body.text: bhyaś cittaṁ vimucyate| (4) tataḥ paraṁ jñeyalakṣaṇaṁ
body.translated_text: is liberated from the obscurations (<s>āvaraṇas</s>). (4) Then, having penetrated the characteristics of the knowable,
the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) of the preliminary practice
should be practiced through realization, relying on a purified superior intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>). (5) Then,
the six <s>pāramitās</s>, embraced by the purified superior intention, should be cultivated
in the ten stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) in their divisions, for three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (<s>trikalpāsaṁkhyeya</s>). (6-8)
Then, the three <s>bodhisattva</s> trainings (<s>śikṣās</s>) should be fulfilled.
(9-10) Having fulfilled them, the fruit of that — <s>nirvāṇa</s> and unsurpassed perfect
awakening (<s>anuttarasamyaksaṁbodhi</s>) — should be fully awakened to. Thus the order of these ten
topics has been taught.
In this teaching, the entire <s>Mahāyāna</s> is complete.
Chapter I (<s>Jñeyāśraya</s> — The Basis of the Knowable)

body.text: tatra tāvat prathamata eva jñeyāśraya ukta ālayavijñā-
body.translated_text: Therein, first of all, the basis of the knowable is stated to be the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>
(storehouse consciousness). Where has the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>
under the designation '<s>ālayavijñāna</s>'? — The <s>Bhagavān</s> has stated in a verse of the <s>Abhidharma-sūtra</s>:
The beginningless element (<s>dhātu</s>) is the common basis of all <s>dharmas</s>;

body.text: tasmin sati gatiḥ sarvā nirvāṇādhigamo 'pi ca||
body.translated_text: because of it, all destinies (<s>gatis</s>) exist, as well as the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
Thus.
Moreover, in that same [<s>sūtra</s>] it is stated:
Consciousness, the seed of all, is attached (<s>ālīna</s>) to all <s>dharmas</s>;
therefore, I have taught the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> to the virtuous.
Thus. This is the scriptural authority (<s>āgama</s>).

body.text: kiṁ kāraṇaṁ tu tad ālayavijñānam ity ucyate| -
body.translated_text: For what reason is it called <s>ālayavijñāna</s>? —
Because all <s>dharmas</s> pertaining to rebirth and defilement are attached (<s>ālīna</s>) to it

body.text: bhāvena tac ca teṣv ālīnaṁ hetubhāvenety ālayavijñānam|
body.translated_text: as their fruit, and it is attached to them as their cause — hence <s>ālayavijñāna</s>.

body.text: atha vā sattvās tadālīnā ātmatvenety ālayavijñānam|
body.translated_text: Or, because beings are attached to it as [their] self — hence <s>ālayavijñāna</s>.

body.text: tac cādānavijñānam ity apy ucyate| atrāgamaḥ| yatho-
body.translated_text: It is also called <s>ādānavijñāna</s> (appropriating consciousness). Here is the scriptural authority. As stated
in the <s>Saṁdhinirmocana-sūtra</s>:
The <s>ādānavijñāna</s>, deep and subtle, flows like a torrent,
bearing all seeds.

body.text: bālāna eṣo mayi na prakāśi(te) mā haiva ātmā
body.translated_text: I have not taught it to the childish, lest
they imagine it as a self. Thus. (<s>Triṁśikā</s>)

body.text: kiṁ kāraṇam ādānavijñānam ity ucyate| - (a) sarva-
body.translated_text: For what reason is it called <s>ādānavijñāna</s>? — Because (a) it appropriates all
material sense faculties, and (b) because it is the basis for the appropriation of all states of existence.

body.text: ca| tathā hi (a) tena pañcarūpindriyāny upādīyante 'vinā-
body.translated_text: For (a) by it the five material sense faculties are appropriated without

body.text: śāya yāvad āyur anuvartate| (b) pratisaṁdhibandhe ca
body.translated_text: destruction for as long as life continues. (b) And at the binding of rebirth (<s>pratisaṁdhi</s>),
a state of existence is appropriated by the appropriation of its production — thus it
is called <s>ādānavijñāna</s>.

body.text: tac ca cittam ity apy ucyate| yathoktaṁ bhagavatā cittaṁ
body.translated_text: It is also called <s>citta</s> (mind). As stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: '<s>citta</s>,
<s>manas</s>, and <s>vijñāna</s>.'
Therein, <s>manas</s> is twofold: (1) Because it serves as the immediately antecedent
condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>) — the consciousness that has just ceased is called <s>manas</s>,

body.text: nasyotpādāśrayaḥ| (2) dvitīyaṁ ca kliṣṭaṁ manaś catur-
body.translated_text: which is the basis for the arising of [new] consciousness. (2) The second is the afflicted <s>manas</s> (<s>kliṣṭa-manas</s>),

body.text: bhiḥ kleśaiḥ sadā samprayuktaṁ satkāyadṛṣṭyā cāsmimā-
body.translated_text: always associated with four afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) — the view of a self-entity (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), the conceit 'I am'

body.text: nena cātmasnehena cāvidyāyā ca| etad vijñānasya saṁkle-
body.translated_text: (<s>asmimāna</s>), self-love (<s>ātmasneha</s>), and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). This is the basis of
defilement of consciousness.

body.text: vijñānaṁ yad ekenāśrayenotpadyate dvitīyena tu saṁkli-
body.translated_text: Consciousness arises from one basis and is defiled by the second.
It is called <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) because of cognizing objects.
<s>Manas</s> is twofold: from immediate [cessation] and from mentation.
I.7A

body.text: kathaṁ punar gamyate tat kliṣṭaṁ mana astīti| tasminn
body.translated_text: How is it known that the afflicted <s>manas</s> (<s>kliṣṭa-manas</s>) exists? In its absence:
(1) there would be the fault of the non-existence of a distinctive ignorance (<s>āveṇikī avidyā</s>); (2) there would be the

body.text: cabhiś ca sādharmyābhāvadoṣo bhavet| tathā hi pañcavij-
body.translated_text: fault of the non-existence of similarity with the five [sense-consciousnesses]. For the five
classes of consciousness have coexisting bases such as the eye, etc. (3) There would be the fault
of the non-existence of an etymology (<s>nirukti</s>); (4) and there would be the fault of the non-existence of a distinction

body.text: viśeṣābhāvadoṣo bhavet| tathā hy asaṁjñisamāpattiḥ kli-
body.translated_text: between the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) and the unconscious attainment (<s>asaṁjñisamāpatti</s>). For the unconscious attainment is

body.text: ṣṭamanasā prabhāvitā na tu nirodhasamāpattiḥ| anyathā
body.translated_text: produced by the afflicted <s>manas</s>, but not the attainment of cessation. Otherwise,

body.text: tayor viśeṣo na syāt| (5) āsaṁjñikāyāṁ caikajātāv akliṣṭa-
body.translated_text: there would be no distinction between the two. (5) In the realm of unconscious beings (<s>āsaṁjñika</s>), in a single birth, there would be the fault of non-affliction,

body.text: tvadoṣo bhaved yadi tatrāhaṁkāro 'smimānaś ca na bha-
body.translated_text: if the sense of 'I' (<s>ahaṁkāra</s>) and the conceit 'I am' (<s>asmimāna</s>) did not exist
there. (6) The activity of the sense of 'I' is always observed
in wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states of mind. Otherwise, the affliction of the conceit 'I am' would arise only with unwholesome mind,

body.text: ṁprayuktatvād asmimānakleśaḥ samudācaren na tu kuśa-
body.translated_text: since it would be associated only with that, and would not
arise with wholesome and indeterminate [states]. Therefore, through coexisting activity and

body.text: samudācāreṇa ca ete doṣā na bhavanti|
body.translated_text: associated activity, these faults do not arise.
I.7B
Here are verses:
The non-existence of a distinctive ignorance, of similarity with the five,
of a distinction in attainment, and of an etymology — [these would be] faults. (1)
The non-existence of the sense of 'I' in the unconscious realm and in the stream of birth [would also be] a fault;
and the accompaniment of the sense of 'I' in all [mental states] would be inexplicable. (2)
Without the <s>kliṣṭamanas</s> (afflicted mind), there would be the non-existence of the two [types of self-grasping] and a contradiction with the three [types of consciousness].

body.text: tasminn asati sarvatra cāhaṁkāro na bhavati|| (3)
body.translated_text: In its absence, <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-consciousness) would not exist anywhere. (3)
It is always an obstruction to the activity of the <s>citta</s> (mind) with respect to its object,
and at all times it is co-existent. <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is regarded as its distinctive [characteristic]. (4)
I. 7C

body.text: manaḥ kliṣṭatvān nivṛtāvyākṛtaṁ kleśaiś caturbhiḥ sadā
body.translated_text: The <s>manas</s> (mind), being afflicted, is <s>nivṛtāvyākṛta</s> (obscured-indeterminate), always
associated with four <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Just as the afflictions of the form and formless realms (<s>rūpa</s> and <s>ārūpya-avacara</s>) are obscured-
indeterminate — because the form and formless realm is embraced by <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) — so too the <s>manas</s>,
because it is bound [to the mind] at all times.
A third <s>citta-śarīra</s> (mind-body) is not apprehended without the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store consciousness).

body.text: reṇa| tena siddham ālayavijñānasya cittatvam| tasmāt
body.translated_text: By that, the nature of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store consciousness) as <s>citta</s> (mind) is established. Therefore,
from that [<s>ālayavijñāna</s>] which contains all seeds (<s>sarvabījaka</s>), <s>manas</s> (mind) and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) arise.

body.text: tac ca kiṁkāraṇaṁ cittam ity apy ucyate| citradharma-
body.translated_text: And for what reason is it also called <s>citta</s> (mind)? Because of the variegated <s>dharma</s>-
<s>vāsanā</s> (impressions) and <s>bījas</s> (seeds) that have been accumulated (<s>ācita</s>) in it.
